**Codex (Frontend Engineer · Pragmatist) — Round 2**

I want to call this `BLOCKED` for build start, but only on a narrow set of real product gaps, not the whole pipeline.

I’m aligned with Codex that the architecture and ownership model are coherent, and I agree with most of Claude’s pressure points too. The one thing I won’t carry as a hard block is the `requirement_ids` issue — that’s a traceability repair, not a product correctness blocker. We can resolve it as a parallel pre-flight task before milestone review, without freezing T-000 if the team wants motion. I do think it should be fixed in the same day and before first merge gate.

What actually blocks correctness now is two concrete inconsistencies from earlier phases that are still not reflected in current execution artifacts. First, resume/corruption flows are still not part of the active flows contract in the same way as earlier locks required: we still need explicit coverage for “resume in-progress game without re-deal” and “semantically invalid save -> fresh deal recovery banner.” Without these, we’re leaving high-risk state transitions untested by design even though they were intentionally locked. Second, the current task contracts don’t force a real card-back selection value proposition: the Settings picker exists, but without a minimum of two distinct backs it can silently become a no-op control, which is exactly the placeholder behavior this gate was built to prevent.

I’m persuaded by Claude’s card-back and gameStarted timing additions, and they’re worth locking before T-008/T-013 gets baked. If `CardBackPicker` ships with one option, it violates user-visible behavior. If `gameStarted` can fire on resume/foreground, stats drift is guaranteed and the app will lie about user effort. We can keep the rule simple and cheap: `gameStarted` only on fresh deal entry points (first launch no restore or explicit New Game / draw-mode confirmation), never on resume. Also add the two-back minimum now, with clear visual distinction, one canonical default + one alternate.

For the legibility gate, I’d keep the existing hard dependency (`T-021` before `T-022`+) because that’s the critical integration guardrail, but I’ll tighten it by requiring an auditable artifact: `CardGalleryDebugView` rendered at actual on-device width with accessibility type, and a recorded PASS/FAIL in the gate notes before proceeding. No external scoring tool is required, but a screenshot artifact tied to the decision is required so it can’t be handwaved.

Given that, I’d settle scope as:
- Build: one app, Game/Stats/Settings only, no live drag, no share sheet, no extra variants.
- No new architecture changes.
- Path convention locked now as `SolitaireAtelier/` in scaffold + module ownership to avoid drift (`SolitaireAtelier/App`, `DesignSystem`, `Domain`, etc.).

The concrete fixes before implementation proceeds: add two missing flows to `flows-json` and their corresponding UI tests, update `T-013`/`T-008` semantics for `gameStarted`, enforce at least 2 card backs and make picker non-placeholder, and add a mandatory `CardGalleryDebugView` artifact gate.

Acceptance gates I’m requiring before merge out of scaffolding: resume path proves no cold-start re-deal on valid resume; corrupt restore path proves fresh-deal recovery + banner; gameStarted fires only on fresh deal start; CardBackPicker has at least 2 selectable backs; no gameplay UI task starts until legibility artifact PASS is recorded; and all major flows in the final flows contract map to explicit UI tests including resume/recovery.

**Claude (Delivery Lead · User Advocate) — Round 2**

Codex, you got me on the flows gap — that's not a matter of interpretation, it's a straight-up regression. I went back and checked: my own draft in the task_assignments phase had F-002 ("Resume in-progress game, no replay") and F-007 ("Simulated corrupt save recovery") sitting right there in the flows-json, and somewhere between that draft and what got stamped as the phase's final locked output, both of them got dropped down to the eight flows that made it through — cold launch, win, stuck, draw-mode change, stats empty state, card-back switch, undo, timer-off. Nobody removed them on purpose; they just didn't survive the last edit pass. And you're right that this isn't a nice-to-have — design_discussion locked the entire non-blocking recovery-banner behavior specifically because a returning player's very first view after a crash or corrupt save is the least forgiving moment in the app (no menu screen to hide behind), and detailed_discussion locked "no replay on resumed cold launch" as its own numbered decision. If those two flows aren't in the actual flows-json that XCUITest gets built against, there's a real chance T-031 ships without a test that ever exercises them, and we'd only find out the recovery banner is broken during human verification instead of catching it mechanically. So: yes, add them back, and I'd map them concretely — "Resume mid-game without replay" asserts the deal/flip animation does NOT play and the board matches pre-kill state exactly (tableau, undo count, elapsed time), and "Corrupt save recovery" asserts the deal/flip DOES play (because RestoreIntegrityService routed it to fresh-deal), followed by the dismissible RecoveryBanner appearing after the deal settles, never before. Both need accessibility-identifier hooks the same way the other eight do.

On requirement-ID reconciliation, I want to actually walk back part of my position, because thinking about it more, I conflated two different costs. I was treating "reconcile against requirements.json" as if it meant reopening a multi-day audit that would stall T-000 — but app_features phase explicitly says it finalized "a 35-item requirements-json," which means the file exists, it was produced, it's just that the task_assignments agent didn't have it in its context window when building the backlog. If the file already exists, this isn't a research task, it's a mechanical diff: take the 33 core R-IDs from that file, map them onto the already-well-organized 33-task backlog (which is thorough enough that the mapping should mostly be 1:1 or close to it), and flag anything uncovered. That's genuinely fast, and Codex is right that skipping it risks masking a real gap — if there's a core requirement in that file with no task anywhere referencing it, we would only find out during final verification, which is a much more expensive place to discover a hole than right now. So here's where I land: it doesn't need to block T-000 itself, since T-000 is pure scaffolding and touches zero requirement IDs, but it does need to complete and be corrected before any other task can be marked done against its acceptance criteria — so it runs in parallel with T-000, not serialized in front of it, but it's a real gate on everything from T-001 onward, not a someday-cleanup item. I think that's a fair synthesis of both our positions rather than a full concession to either "blocks everything" or "doesn't matter."

I'm holding firm on the three things I raised, since nobody's pushed back on them yet and I think they're real. The card-back count one in particular — I want to make sure this doesn't get waved off as a nitpick, because it's exactly the kind of thing that reads as "done" on paper (CardBackPicker compiles, T-026's acceptance criteria technically pass) while actually being a broken feature in a screenshot-worthy app that's supposed to be judged on exactly this kind of polish. Two card backs, final, so the picker is a real picker. Same logic on gameStarted — I'd rather over-specify "fires once per fresh deal, never on resume, never on foreground" now than have services_utilities interpret "session start" as "app becomes active" and quietly inflate every stats number on the one screen whose entire job is being honest. And on the legibility gate, since this has been flagged as unresolved risk in every single phase back to product_research, I don't think it's acceptable to let this round pass without pinning an actual verification mechanism — "manual pass recorded" is not a mechanism, it's a hope. Wiring CardGalleryDebugView's output through the same screenshot-scoring pipeline this fleet already uses (the one that caught blank-screen failures elsewhere per the anti-patterns log) turns this from a vibe check into an actual gate artifact, and the bounded fallback (flatten only the corner-index/pip zone to solid ink if it fails, don't touch the rest of the card) means a FAIL doesn't turn into an open-ended redesign that eats the schedule project_plan already admitted has zero slack for.

One more small thing to close since Codex raised it and it's genuinely a two-minute fix: lock the actual folder name now, at T-000, so it stops being ambiguous. I'd go with `SolitaireAtelier/` as the Xcode project/target name (matches Swift type-naming conventions like `SolitaireAtelierApp.swift` that are already locked everywhere in the task list) while the outer working-directory slug stays `solitaire-atelier` — that's not a conflict, it's just an app-name-vs-repo-slug distinction that's extremely common and doesn't need reconciling, it needs stating explicitly in T-000's acceptance criteria so no lane invents a third variant. I don't think this needs more debate, just a sentence in the final output.

So where I think we actually are: architecture's fine, nobody's found a real contradiction there, and the punch list to close before code is short — restore the two missing flows, do the fast R-ID diff in parallel with T-000 (not blocking it, but gating everything after), lock two card backs, lock gameStarted-on-fresh-deal-only, lock the screenshot-scored legibility mechanism with its bounded fallback, and pin the SolitaireAtelier/solitaire-atelier naming split in T-000. None of that is scope creep or new features — it's closing gaps that were already implied by decisions everyone already agreed to, just never made concrete enough for a build lane to implement without guessing.

**Readiness verdict:** Not blocked on architecture — every upstream phase (prompt contract, design handoff, tech specs, architecture review, project plan, task assignments) is internally consistent. Build start is gated on six concrete, cheap fixes, not a redesign or re-plan.

**Required fixes before/alongside build start:**

1. **Restore the two dropped flows.** `flows-json` lost "resume in-progress game without re-deal" and "corrupt save recovery" somewhere after task_assignments' draft. Both must be added back with concrete assertions: resume asserts no deal/flip animation plays and board state (tableau, undo count, elapsed time) matches exactly pre-kill; corrupt-recovery asserts the deal/flip *does* play (fresh deal via RestoreIntegrityService routing) followed by a dismissible RecoveryBanner appearing only after the deal settles. Both get accessibility-identifier hooks like the other eight flows and corresponding XCUITest cases in T-031.
2. **Requirement-ID reconciliation is real but fast, and non-blocking for T-000 only.** The actual requirements.json exists (app_features produced 33 core + 2 non-core R-IDs) — task_assignments just didn't have it in context. This is a mechanical diff/mapping task, not an audit. It runs in parallel with T-000 (scaffolding doesn't reference any R-ID) but must complete and be corrected before any task from T-001 onward can be marked done against its acceptance criteria.
3. **Card-back minimum locked at exactly two:** one canonical Baize & Vellum back plus one clearly visually distinct alternate. `CardBackPicker` must ship as a real picker, not a single-option control masquerading as one.
4. **`gameStarted` firing semantics locked:** fires exactly once per genuinely fresh deal (first launch with no valid restore, or an explicit New Game / draw-mode-change confirmation) — never on a resumed cold launch, never on foregrounding an already-active session. This is binding on T-008/T-013.
5. **Legibility gate gets a real artifact, not a vibe check.** `CardGalleryDebugView` must render at the actual on-device `cardWidth()` output through accessibility1 Dynamic Type, captured as a screenshot artifact, with a recorded PASS/FAIL tied to that artifact before any task depending on T-021 proceeds. A bounded fallback is pre-approved if it fails: flatten the corner-index/center-pip zone to solid ink only (larger index, bolder stroke) — not a full glyph-system redesign, since project_plan's schedule has no slack for one.
6. **Naming split pinned in T-000:** Xcode project/target is named `SolitaireAtelier/` (matching the already-locked Swift file conventions like `SolitaireAtelierApp.swift`); the outer working-directory/repo slug stays `solitaire-atelier`. This is a stated convention, not a conflict to resolve.

**Final scope for build:** unchanged from task_assignments — one app, Game/Stats/Settings triad, draw-1 and draw-3 both fully working, no live interactive drag, no win-screen share sheet, no extra card-back variants beyond the locked two, no third-party dependencies, no architecture changes.

**Acceptance criteria checklist for build to proceed:**
- flows-json contains all 10 flows (8 existing + resume-no-replay + corrupt-save-recovery), each mapped to a passing XCUITest.
- Requirement-ID diff against the real requirements.json completed and any gap flagged before T-001 is accepted as done.
- `CardBackPicker` has ≥2 selectable, visually distinct backs.
- `gameStarted` event logic verified to fire only on fresh-deal entry points, never on resume/foreground.
- `CardGalleryDebugView` screenshot artifact captured and PASS recorded before T-022 onward may start (FAIL triggers the named bounded fallback, not an open redesign).
- T-000 acceptance criteria explicitly state the `SolitaireAtelier`/`solitaire-atelier` naming convention.
- All previously-locked gates carry forward unchanged: T-021→T-022+ hard dependency, `GameEngine.swift`/`SolitaireAtelierApp.swift` integrator-owned files, per-lane testing ownership, zero-third-party-dependency CI gate.
